elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 contains a mutual CGL requirement, but the cited/rendered text does not display the CGL sub-clause and its limits are redacted ([***]), so no USD 1,000,000 per-occurrence floor can be verified; the redline adds nothing on CGL.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Same redaction problem: the aggregate CGL limit is not visible in the operative language ([***] limits), and the inserted sentence addresses only E&O and cyber.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted language sets SFJ E&O at "a minimum limit of one million dollars ($1,000,000)", below the preferred USD 2,000,000; existing 12.3.2.4 imposes professional liability only on subcontractors and at a redacted limit.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted cyber and privacy liability limit is "two million dollars ($2,000,000)", short of the preferred USD 5,000,000; no other cyber cover exists in the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation provision appears in the rendered operative language; 12.3.2 lists types of cover but the enumerated sub-clauses other than 12.3.2.4 are not before us, so presence cannot be confirmed, and the redline does not add it.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts Section 12.3 already includes certificates on request, but no certificate language appears in the rendered operative text, so it cannot be verified from the clause as rendered.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: New paragraph: "SFJ will maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with a minimum limit of one million dollars ($1,000,000)" — an SFJ-level obligation, curing the subcontractor-only scope of 12.3.2.4.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: New paragraph: "cyber and privacy liability insurance with a minimum limit of two million dollars ($2,000,000)" imposed directly on SFJ; no prior cyber cover existed.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: both atomic elements (E&O USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000) are carried by a single new sentence imposing the obligation directly on the counterparty (SFJ), not merely on subcontractors, so the clause is position-complete at the fallback.

Preferred level is not reached: E&O is USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000 and cyber is USD 2,000,000 rather than USD 5,000,000; CGL per-occurrence/aggregate limits and workers' compensation cannot be verified because the existing limits are redacted ([***]) and those sub-clauses are not in the rendered text. If the preferred position is pursued, raise the inserted E&O figure to USD 2,000,000 and cyber to USD 5,000,000 and add express CGL USD 1M/2M, workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion of new words for an otherwise missing coverage type, with no deletions, no survival tail, no "at its own expense" language, no certificate or notice procedures, and no other limits disturbed — nothing beyond the two selected fallback elements was added.

Intent preserved: the mutual 12.3.2 structure, the greater-of Applicable Law floor, the subcontractor professional liability requirement in 12.3.2.4 and its tail period all survive unchanged; the new sentence names SFJ expressly, so it does not contradict the "each Party" chapeau, and it leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.
Drafting nit (not a defect against the checklist): the insertion is untitled/unnumbered within the 12.3.2 enumeration — consider numbering it 12.3.2.x so it sits cleanly in the list.
